question.problem: Given that the continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-3,1],$ compute $P(-2\le X\le 2).$

current_example.problem: Given that the continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-1, 4],$ compute $P(0<   X <  3).$
current_example.worked_solution:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $X$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14128799/assets/7dd784ec8ea8db9624cd9c945bc8f8e84fd2cbce263f9d19f4506f5417c8f85b.svg)

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-1,4],$ so it has the following probability density function:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14128799/assets/a42eebe866206e69fe64d993746d7e3428a6d1673f27ed92f9a36eed346fc1b6.svg)

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0<X<3) & =P(0<X<3) \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3-0}{5} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
